A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same MAB-N framework and estimation-regret trade-off. Their complete main texts, mathematical material, figures, tables, and appendices support comparison; relocated and renumbered content can be matched.

before.justification: v1 contains theoretical results, proofs, algorithm descriptions, and a schematic Pareto-frontier figure, but no original empirical outcomes, including in its appendices.

after.justification: v2 Appendix D reports original simulations on a 101-unit network. Figure 3 presents cumulative regret and ATE estimation errors for three policies, with 1,000 executions reported per policy.

M1.justification: The two-stage UCB and EXP3 procedures remain. Algorithm 1 changes the coefficient under the UCB bonus square root from 9 to 18, and Algorithm 2 permits a prespecified conditional sampling distribution instead of requiring uniform sampling. Appendix L also adds an optional nearest-feasible-exposure replacement procedure.

E1.justification: v2 introduces the paper's first empirical coverage: regret minimization and treatment-effect estimation on a synthetic binary-treatment network with 101 units in six clusters. v1 discusses such tasks theoretically but evaluates no simulated or real dataset.

E2.justification: Appendix D adds the first empirical comparator set: Standard, defined as UCB-TSN with T1 = 0, and Uniform, with T1 = T. The existing analytical comparison with Simchi-Levi and Wang's EXP3EG remains; that method is not included in the new simulation.

E3.justification: The new simulation establishes an empirical protocol using binary actions, thresholded neighbor exposure, uniform sampling of compatible assignments, and Bernoulli rewards. It compares exploration lengths of zero, sqrt(|UE|T), and T using cumulative regret and maximum ATE error; Figure 3's regret curves extend to 10,000 rounds.

E4.justification: The Standard and Uniform comparisons provide a focused ablation of the exploration phase, testing its removal and extension to the entire horizon against the proposed intermediate duration. This analysis is confined to one synthetic network.

E5.justification: v2 newly reports 1,000 executions per algorithm, averaged results, and ATE-error box plots showing medians, interquartile ranges, and outliers. v1 has no empirical uncertainty reporting. Seeds and a confidence-interval or significance-testing procedure are not specified.

E6.justification: Figure 3 adds the first empirical findings. Its curves show Standard with the lowest cumulative regret, UCB-TSN intermediate, and Uniform highest. Uniform and UCB-TSN show smaller, less dispersed ATE errors than Standard. The accompanying description that both Standard and UCB-TSN achieve the lowest regret overstates their equivalence.

T1.justification: The principal asymptotic rates remain, but Appendix G substantially revises the lower-bound construction and testing argument. Appendix H adds a necessity argument under polynomial-rate restrictions, whereas v1's corresponding appendix proves sufficiency only. Appendix L introduces optimization formulations and modified exposure-reward definitions for infeasible cluster-wise exposures.

C1.justification: The central framework, trade-off, and algorithmic-achievability claims remain. However, v1 advertises an if-and-only-if Pareto characterization, while v2 explicitly identifies the main theorem as sufficient and treats necessity under additional polynomial-rate assumptions in Appendix H, Remark 10.

C2.justification: Appendix L newly discusses the potentially NP-hard search for feasible exposure assignments and applicability when Condition 1 fails, extending an issue previously deferred to future work. Appendix D also attributes Standard's poorer estimation to insufficient exploration of suboptimal arms.

D1.justification: Appendix D supplies concrete cluster memberships, the exposure threshold, assignment-sampling rule, reward family, and exploration settings. Appendix L recommends mixed-integer nonlinear optimization for exposure feasibility. These are useful additions, but the simulation's Bernoulli means and implementation resources are not supplied.

R1.justification: The main positioning against interference-aware bandits and estimation-regret trade-off research remains. The new main-text related-work section largely draws on existing Appendix B, while references such as Belotti et al., Sekhon, Hudgens and Halloran, and Sävje extend the discussion and new comparison table.

P1.justification: The introduction and framework receive extensive rewriting and expanded explanations. v2 adds a main-text related-work section and proof sketch, reorganizes the framework and conditions, and moves the exposure justification and node-number discussion into appendices. The narrative structure changes substantially.

P2.justification: v2 substantially expands the visual presentation with a network diagram, empirical regret curves and error box plots, and a literature-comparison table. Table 1 moves to the appendix and gains a single-unit comparison row and estimation-goal column; the notation table is reformatted. The original Pareto illustration is retained.

improvement.justification: v2 improves exposition, aligns the UCB bonus with the existing regret proof, qualifies the necessity claim, and adds a useful repeated-run illustration of the trade-off. The overall gain is limited by the single synthetic setting, missing Bernoulli reward parameters, and the overstated regret comparison in Appendix D. The additions improve clarity and supporting evidence without establishing substantially stronger overall validation.
